record.summary: Risk-based AI bill drawing on EU, US and Chinese laws. Before a system is marketed or put into service, its provider would carry out a preliminary evaluation to classify its risk level; applications with excessive risk would be prohibited and high-risk applications would face stricter controls. The bill sets transparency and bias-mitigation measures, with additional measures for high-risk and government AI systems, and an algorithmic impact assessment procedure. Affected persons would have rights to prior information about interacting with AI, explanation of decisions, challenge of decisions with legal or significant effects, human participation, non-discrimination and data protection.
